Tompkins Financial Corporation ("Tompkins" or the "Company") is headquartered in Ithaca, New York and is registered as a Financial Holding Company with the Federal Reserve Board under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. The Company is a locally-oriented, community-based financial services organization that offers a full array of products and services, including commercial and consumer banking, leasing, trust and investment management, financial planning and wealth management services. At December 31, 2025, the Company had one wholly-owned banking subsidiary, Tompkins Community Bank. Banking services consist primarily of attracting deposits from the areas served by Tompkins Community Bank's 54 banking offices (38 offices in New York and 16 offices in Pennsylvania), and using those deposits to originate a variety of commercial loans, agricultural loans, consumer loans, real estate loans, and leases in those same areas. Tompkins Community Bank provides a full array of trust and wealth management services under the Tompkins Financial Advisors brand, including investment management, trust and estate, financial and tax planning. The Company previously provided insurance services through its wholly-owned insurance subsidiary, Tompkins Insurance Agencies, Inc. ("TIA"), but on October 31, 2025, the Company sold all of the issued and outstanding shares of the capital stock of TIA, to Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC ("Gallagher"). The Company's principal offices are located at 118 E. Seneca St., P.O. Box 460, Ithaca, New York, 14850, and its telephone number is (888) 503-5753. The Company's common stock is traded on the NYSE American under the symbol "TMP."

Tompkins was organized in 1995, under the laws of the State of New York, as a bank holding company for Tompkins Trust Company (the "Trust Company"), a commercial bank that has operated in Ithaca, New York and surrounding communities since 1836. In January 2021, Tompkins combined its four wholly-owned banking subsidiaries into one bank, with the Bank of Castile, Mahopac Bank, and VIST Bank merging with and into the Trust Company. Immediately following the merger, the Trust Company changed its name to Tompkins Community Bank.

The Tompkins strategy centers around its core values and a commitment to delivering long-term value to our clients, communities, and shareholders. A key strategic initiative for the Company is a focus on responsible and sustainable growth, including initiatives to grow organically through our current businesses, as well as through possible acquisitions of financial institutions, branches, and financial services businesses. As such, the Company has acquired, and from time to time considers acquiring, banks, thrift institutions, branch offices of banks or thrift institutions, or other businesses that would complement the Company's business or its geographic reach. The Company generally targets merger or acquisition partners that are culturally similar and have experienced management and possess either significant market presence or have potential for improved profitability through financial management, economies of scale and expanded services. The Company has pursued acquisition opportunities in the past, and continues to review new opportunities.

The Company also has defined strategic initiatives around digital delivery of services to meet the changing needs of client expectations, while maintaining our commitment to excellence in the delivery of personal service when self-serve options are unable to meet the needs of our clients. Our strategy includes a focus on building a scalable foundation based on a continuous improvement approach necessary for our long-term success. This foundation includes investments in automation, analytics and security to drive ongoing consistency, efficiency, and security in our operations. We also recognize the need to develop and acquire talent that is well prepared to succeed in our changing industry. Initiatives in this area include a focus on characteristics such as collaboration, innovation and agility.
The Company has identified two business segments, consisting of banking and wealth management. Prior to its sale of TIA on October 31, 2025, the Company also had an insurance segment.

Banking services consist primarily of attracting deposits from the areas served by the Company's banking subsidiary and using those deposits to originate a variety of commercial loans, agricultural loans, consumer loans, real estate loans, and leases in those same market areas. The Company's lending function is managed within the guidelines of a comprehensive Board of Directors-approved lending policy. Policies and procedures are reviewed on a regular basis. Reporting systems are in place to provide management with ongoing information related to loan production, loan quality, concentrations of credit, loan

delinquencies and nonperforming and potential problem loans. The Company has an independent third party loan review process that samples, reviews, and validates the risk identification and assessment made by the lenders and credit personnel. The results of these reviews are presented to the Board of Directors of the Company's banking subsidiary, and the bank's Credit Oversight Committee.

The Company's principal expenses are interest on deposits, interest on borrowings, and operating and general administrative expenses, as well as provisions for credit loss expenses. Funding sources other than deposits, include borrowings, securities sold under agreements to repurchase, and cash flow from lending and investing activities. The Company's principal source of revenue is interest income on loans and securities.

The Company maintains a portfolio of securities such as U.S. Treasury securities, obligations of U.S. government agencies and U.S. government sponsored entities, obligations of states and political subdivisions thereof, and equity securities. Management typically invests in securities with short to intermediate average lives in order to better match the interest rate sensitivities of its assets and liabilities. Investment decisions are made within policy guidelines established by the Company's Board of Directors. The investment policy is based on the asset/liability management goals of the Company, and is monitored by the Company's Asset/Liability Management Committee. The intent of the policy is to establish a portfolio of high quality diversified securities, which optimizes net interest income within safety and liquidity limits deemed acceptable by the Asset/Liability Management Committee.

Wealth management services consist of investment management, trust and estate, financial and tax planning as well as life, disability and long-term care insurance services. Wealth management services are provided under the trade name Tompkins Financial Advisors.

The Company operated its wholly-owned insurance subsidiary, TIA, from 2001 until its sale to Gallagher on October 31, 2025. TIA was a full-service insurance agency that offered services such as property and casualty insurance, employee benefit consulting, and life, long-term care and disability insurance. TIA's revenue and expenses are consolidated into the Company's financials through October 31, 2025.

Tompkins Community Bank operates 54 branches, with 38 branches located in New York, and 16 located in Pennsylvania. Tompkins has operated in Ithaca, New York and surrounding communities since 1836. Tompkins Community Bank provides a full array of products and services, including commercial and consumer banking. Tompkins Community Bank also provides wealth management services, including investment management, trust and estate, financial and tax planning services, through the Tompkins Financial Advisors brand. As of December 31, 2025, Tompkins Community Bank had consolidated total assets of $8.7 billion, consolidated total loans of $6.4 billion, and consolidated total deposits of $7.1 billion. A description of the markets served by Tompkins Community Bank is included below:

We operate 12 branches in our CNY market, with the largest market area being Tompkins County, which has a population of approximately 104,000. Education plays a significant role in the Tompkins County economy with Cornell University and Ithaca College being two of the county's major employers. Tompkins Community Bank has a full-service office in Cortland, New York and a full-service office in Auburn, New York. Both of these offices are located in counties contiguous to Tompkins County. Tompkins Community Bank also has two full-service branches in Fayetteville and Syracuse, New York, which are located in Onondaga County.

paragraphs: The Company's success depends on management's ability to identify and manage the risks inherent in its financial services business. These risks include credit risk, market risk, liquidity risk, operational risk, regulatory, compliance and legal risk, and strategic risk. We list below the material risks we face. Any of these risks could result in a material adverse impact on the Company's business, operating results, financial condition, liquidity, and cash flow, or may cause the Company's results to vary materially from recent results, or from the results implied by any forward-looking statements made by the Company.

The Company is subject to increased business risk because the Company has a significant concentration of commercial real estate and commercial business loans, repayment of which is often dependent on the cash flows of the borrower.

The Company offers different types of commercial loans to a variety of businesses, and we believe commercial loans will continue to comprise a significant concentration of our loan portfolio in 2026 and beyond. Real estate lending is generally considered to be collateral-based lending with loan amounts based on predetermined loan-to-collateral values. As such, declines in real estate valuations in the Company's market area would lower the value of the collateral securing these loans. Additionally, the Company has experienced, and expects to continue experiencing, increased competition in commercial real estate lending. This increased competition may inhibit the Company's ability to generate additional commercial real estate loans or maintain its current inventory of commercial real estate loans. The Company's commercial business loans are made based primarily on the cash flow and creditworthiness of the borrower and secondarily on the underlying collateral provided by the borrower, with liquidation of the underlying real estate collateral being viewed as the primary source of repayment in the event of borrower default. The borrowers' cash flow may be difficult to predict, and collateral securing these loans may fluctuate in value. Although commercial business loans are often collateralized by equipment, inventory, accounts receivable, or other business assets, the liquidation of collateral in the event of default is often an insufficient source of repayment. As of December 31, 2025, commercial and commercial real estate loans totaled $4.8 billion or 73.9% of the Company's total loans.

The Company's agricultural loans are often dependent upon the health of the agricultural industry in the location of the borrower, and the ability of the borrower to repay may be affected by many factors outside of the borrower's control.

As part of the Company's commercial business lending activities, the Company originates agricultural loans, consisting of agricultural real estate loans and agricultural operating loans. As of December 31, 2025, $348.8 million or 5.4% of the Company's total loan portfolio consisted of agriculturally-related loans, including $234.3 million in agricultural real estate loans and $114.5 million in agricultural operating loans. Payments on agricultural loans are dependent on the profitable operation or management of the related farm property. The success of the farm may be affected by many factors outside the control of the borrower, including adverse weather conditions that prevent the planting of a crop or limit crop yields (such as wind, hail, drought and floods), loss of livestock due to disease or other factors, declines in market prices for agricultural products and the impact of governmental regulations and subsidies (including changes in price supports and environmental regulations). Many farms are dependent upon a limited number of key individuals whose injury or death may significantly affect the successful operation of the farm. If the cash flow from a farming operation is diminished, the borrower's ability to repay the loan may be impaired. While agricultural operating loans are generally secured by a blanket lien on the farm's operating assets, any repossessed collateral in respect of a defaulted loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment of the outstanding balance.

Additionally, the profitable operation or management of the related farm properties, and the value thereof, is impacted by changes in U.S. government trade policies. Tariffs, retaliatory tariffs or other trade restrictions on products and materials that farm properties related to our agriculturally-related loans import or export could cause the costs of such farm operations and management to increase, the price of products from such farm operations to increase, demand for such products to decrease and the margins on such products to decrease. Such potential adverse effects on farm property operations and management could reduce the related farm properties' revenues, financial results and ability to service debt, which, in turn, could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. In addition, to the extent changes in the political environment related to the agriculture industry have a negative impact on our customers or on the markets in which we operate, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially and adversely impacted in the future.

The Company is headquartered in Ithaca, New York and is registered as a Financial Holding Company with the Federal Reserve Board under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. The statements contained in this Report that are not statements of historical fact may include forward-looking statements that involve a number of risks and uncertainties. Forward-looking statements may be identified by use of such words as "may", "could", "should", "will", "would", "estimate", "intend", "continue", "believe", "expect", "plan", "commit", or "anticipate", as well as the negative and other variations of these terms, and other similar words. Examples of forward-looking statements may include statements regarding the asset quality of the Company's loan portfolios; the level of the Company's allowance for credit losses; the sufficiency of collateral to cover exposure related to special mention and substandard loans; the sufficiency of liquidity sources; expectations regarding securities revenue in future periods; the Company's exposure to changes in interest rates, and to new, changed, or extended government/regulatory expectations; the need to sell securities before recovery of amortized cost; the impact of changes in accounting standards; trends, plans, prospects, growth and strategies; projections of future financial condition, operating results, income, capital expenditures, costs or other financial items; anticipated regulatory and legislative changes; and other characterizations of future events or circumstances as well as other statements that are not statements of historical fact. Forward-looking statements are made based on management's expectations and beliefs concerning future events impacting the Company and are subject to uncertainties and factors relating to the Company's operations and economic environment, all of which are difficult to predict and many of which are beyond the control of the Company, that could cause actual results of the Company to differ materially from those expressed and/or implied by forward-looking statements and historical performance. The following factors, in addition to those listed as Risk Factors in Item 1A of this Report on Form 10-K, are among those that could cause actual results to differ materially from the forward-looking statements and historical performance: changes in general economic, market and regulatory conditions; our ability to attract and retain deposits and other sources of liquidity; gross domestic product growth and inflation trends; the impact of the interest rate and inflationary environment on the Company's business, financial condition and results of operations; The Company does not undertake any obligation to update its forward-looking statements.

The accounting and reporting policies followed by the Company conform, in all material respects, to U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP") and to general practices within the financial services industry. In the course of normal business

activity, management must select and apply many accounting policies and methodologies and make estimates and assumptions that lead to the financial results presented in the Company's consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. There are uncertainties inherent in making these estimates and assumptions, which could materially affect the Company's results of operations and financial position.

Management considers accounting estimates to be critical to reported financial results if (i) the accounting estimates require management to make assumptions about matters that are highly uncertain, and (ii) different estimates that management reasonably could have used for the accounting estimate in the current period, or changes in the accounting estimate that are reasonably likely to occur from period to period, could have a material impact on the Company's financial statements. Management considers the accounting policies relating to the allowance for credit losses ("allowance", or "ACL") to be a critical accounting policy because of the uncertainty and subjectivity involved in this policy and the material effect that estimates related to this area can have on the Company's financial condition and results of operations.

The Company's methodology for estimating the allowance considers available relevant information about the collectability of cash flows, including information about past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts. Refer to "Allowance for Credit Losses" below, "Note 5 - Allowance for Credit Losses", and "Note 1 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Report on Form 10-K for additional discussion regarding the allowance.

For information on the Company's significant accounting policies and to gain a greater understanding of how the Company's financial performance is reported, refer to "Note 1 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Report on Form 10-K.

The Company's significant accounting policies conform with GAAP and are described in "Note 1 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Report on Form 10-K. In applying those accounting policies, management of the Company is required to exercise judgment in determining many of the methodologies, assumptions and estimates to be utilized. Certain critical accounting estimates are more dependent on such judgment and in some cases may contribute to volatility in the Company's reported financial performance should the assumptions and estimates used change over time due to changes in circumstances. The most significant area in which management of the Company applies critical assumptions and estimates was the following:

•Accounting for credit losses - The Company accounts for the allowance for credit losses using the current expected credit loss model. Under this model, the allowance for credit losses represents a valuation account that is deducted from the amortized cost basis of certain financial assets, including loans and leases, to present the net amount expected to be collected at the balance sheet date. A provision for credit losses is recorded to adjust the level of the allowance as deemed necessary by management. In estimating expected losses in the loan and lease portfolio, borrower-specific financial data and macro-economic assumptions are utilized to project losses over a reasonable and supportable forecast period. For certain loan pools that share similar risk characteristics, the Company utilizes statistically developed models to estimate amounts and timing of expected future cash flows, collateral values and other factors used to determine the borrowers' abilities to repay obligations. Such models consider historical correlations of credit losses with various macroeconomic assumptions including unemployment and gross domestic product. These forecasts may be adjusted for inherent limitations or biases of the models. Subsequent to the forecast period, the Company utilizes longer-term historical loss experience to estimate losses over the remaining contractual life of the loans. Changes in the circumstances considered when determining management's estimates and assumptions could result in changes in those estimates and assumptions, which could result in adjustment of the allowance for credit losses in future periods. A discussion of facts and circumstances considered by management in determining the allowance for credit losses is included herein in "Note 5 - Allowance for Credit Losses" in the Notes to the Unaudited Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Report on Form 10-K.

The Company reported diluted earnings per share of $11.24 in 2025, an increase of 126.2% compared to diluted earnings per share of $4.97 in 2024. Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $161.1 million, an increase of 127.3% compared to $70.9 million in 2024. The increase in both diluted earnings per share and net income included the sale of all of the

issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Tompkins Insurance Agencies, Inc. ("TIA") to Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC. ("Gallagher") for approximately $223.0 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, during the fourth quarter of 2025. The transaction generated a pre-tax gain of $188.2 million recognized in noninterest income. The Company also incurred $4.3 million of expenses related to the sale of TIA, which are included in noninterest expense. Partially offsetting the gain in 2025 was a sale of $564.2 million of available-for-sale debt securities, also during the fourth quarter of 2025, which resulted in an pre-tax loss on the sale of securities of $78.7 million. Management expects this sale to favorably impact securities revenue in future periods as the securities sold had an average yield of 1.56%, while the proceeds of the sale were largely reinvested into securities with an estimated yield of approximately 4.52%.

Excluding the impact of the sale of TIA and realized losses on sales of investment securities, adjusted net income, a non-GAAP financial measure, was $90.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, up $19.6 million, or 27.7%, when compared to the prior year. Earnings per diluted share, adjusted to exclude the impact of the sale of TIA and realized losses on sales of investment securities ("adjusted diluted earnings per share"), also a non-GAAP financial measure, of $6.31 for the year ended December 31, 2025, increased $1.35 or 27.2% compared to the prior year. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures with the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are presented in the "Non-GAAP Disclosure" on page 49.

paragraphs: 本節所述之揭露內容，受本報告第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」所列之「前瞻性陳述」節及本報告其他處所列之警示性陳述所限制。

Tompkins Financial Corporation（"Tompkins" 或 "本公司"）總部設於紐約伊薩卡市，並已向聯邦儲備銀行註冊為根據 1956 年銀行控股公司法（已修正）設立之金融控股公司。本公司為一個以當地為導向、社區為基礎之財務服務機構，提供包括商業與消費者銀行、租賃、信託與投資管理、財務規劃及資產管理服務等完整產品與服務。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有唯一之 wholly-owned 銀行子公司 Tompkins Community Bank。銀行服務主要為吸引來自 Tompkins Community Bank 所服務地區之存款（該銀行設有 54 處分行，其中 38 處位於紐約，16 處位於賓夕法尼亞州），並運用這些存款發放多種商業貸款、農業貸款、消費者貸款、不動產貸款及租賃於相同地區。Tompkins Community Bank 在 Tompkins Financial Advisors 品牌下提供完整之信託與資產管理服務，包括投資管理、信託與遺產規劃、財務與稅務規劃。本公司曾透過其 wholly-owned 保險子公司 Tompkins Insurance Agencies, Inc.（"TIA"）提供保險服務，但於 2025 年 10 月 31 日，本公司已將 TIA 全部已發行且流通之資本股票出售給 Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC（"Gallagher"）。本公司主要辦公室位於紐約伊薩卡市 118 E. Seneca St., P.O. Box 460, 14850，電話號碼為 (888) 503-5753。本公司普通股於 NYSE American 交易，代碼為 "TMP."

Tompkins 於 1995 年根據紐約州法律設立，作為 Tompkins Trust Company（"信託公司"）之銀行控股公司，該信託公司為一家自 1836 年以來在紐約伊薩卡市及其周邊社區營運之商業銀行。於 2021 年 1 月，Tompkins 將其四家 wholly-owned 銀行子公司合併為一家銀行，Bank of Castile、Mahopac Bank 與 VIST Bank 合併進信託公司。合併後立即，信託公司更名為 Tompkins Community Bank。

Tompkins 之策略圍繞其核心價值觀，並致力於為客戶、社區及股東創造長期價值。本公司之關鍵戰略計畫為專注於負責任且可持續的成長，包括透過現有業務進行有機成長，以及透過可能收購金融機構、分行及金融服務業務來實現成長。因此，本公司已收購，並偶爾考慮收購銀行、儲蓄機構、銀行或儲蓄機構之分行或其他業務，以補強本公司業務或其地理範圍。本公司通常尋求文化相近且具備經驗管理階層之合併或收購夥伴，這些夥伴或具備顯著市場佔有率，或具備透過財務管理、規模經濟及擴展服務而改善獲利潛力之潛力。本公司過去曾進行收購機會，並持續評估新機會。

本公司亦已明確界定戰略計畫，以數位方式提供服務，以符合客戶需求的變化，同時維持本公司對個人服務卓越品質的承諾，當自助選項無法滿足客戶需求時。本公司之策略包括專注於建立一個可擴展的基礎，此基礎基於持續改進的觀點，以實現長期成功。此基礎包括對自動化、分析及安全性的投資，以推動運作的持續一致性、效率及安全性。本公司亦認知到培養及取得具備成功經驗之人才的必要性。此領域的計畫包括專注於合作、創新及靈活性等特質。
本公司已識別出兩個業務分部，分別為銀行與資產管理。在 2025 年 10 月 31 日出售 TIA 之前，本公司亦曾有保險業務分部。
銀行服務主要為吸引來自本公司銀行子公司所服務地區之存款，並運用這些存款發放多種商業貸款、農業貸款、消費者貸款、不動產貸款及租賃於相同市場地區。本公司之貸款業務係根據董事會批准之綜合貸款政策進行管理。政策與程序定期進行審查。已設置報告系統，以提供管理層有關貸款發放、貸款品質、信用集中、貸款
逾期與非表現及潛在問題貸款之持續資訊。本公司設有獨立第三方貸款審查程序，該程序會抽樣審查並驗證貸款人及信用人員所進行之風險識別與評估。這些審查結果會呈交本公司銀行子公司董事會，以及銀行之信用監督委員會。
本公司的主要費用為存款利息、借款利息、營運及一般行政費用，以及信貸損失提列費用。除存款外的資金來源，包括借款、根據協議出售之證券、以及貸款及投資活動之現金流。本公司的主要收入來源為貸款及證券之利息收入。

本公司持有包括美國國庫證券、美國政府機構義務、美國政府支持機構義務、州及該州政治子單位義務，以及權益證券等證券組合。管理層通常投資於平均壽命為短至中等的證券，以更好地匹配其資產與負債的利率敏感度。投資決策係在本公司董事會所建立的政策指引範圍內進行。投資政策係基於本公司資產/負債管理目標，並由本公司資產/負債管理委員會監督。此政策的意圖為建立高品質且多元化之證券組合，以在資產/負債管理委員會認為可接受的安全與流動性範圍內，優化淨利息收入。
財富管理服務包括投資管理、信託與遺產、財務與稅務規劃，以及壽險、殘障保險與長期照護保險服務。財富管理服務係以「Tompkins Financial Advisors」商標提供。
本公司自2001年起經營其全資擁有之保險子公司TIA，直至2025年10月31日出售給Gallagher為止。TIA為一家提供全方位保險服務的保險經紀公司，提供如財產與意外保險、員工福利諮詢，以及壽險、長期照護與殘障保險等服務。TIA之收入與費用自2025年10月31日止，已併入本公司財務報表中。

Tompkins Community Bank經營54家分行，其中38家位於紐約州，16家位於賓夕法尼亞州。Tompkins自1836年起便在紐約州伊薩卡市及其周遭社區營運。Tompkins Community Bank提供完整的商業與消費銀行產品與服務。Tompkins Community Bank亦透過「Tompkins Financial Advisors」品牌提供財富管理服務，包括投資管理、信託與遺產、財務與稅務規劃服務。截至2025年12月31日，Tompkins Community Bank之合併總資產為8.7十億美元，合併總貸款為6.4十億美元，合併總存款為7.1十億美元。有關Tompkins Community Bank服務之市場描述如下：

我們在中國大陸市場經營12家分行，其中最大的市場為Tompkins縣，人口約為104,000人。教育在Tompkins縣經濟中扮演重要角色，康奈爾大學與伊薩卡學院為該縣的主要僱主。Tompkins Community Bank在紐約州科爾敦設有全功能辦事處，並在紐約州奧本設有全功能辦事處。這兩個辦事處均位於與Tompkins縣相鄰的縣市。Tompkins Community Bank亦在費耶維爾與雪城設有兩家全功能分行，位於奧農達加縣。

本公司總部設於紐約伊薩卡市，並已向聯邦儲備銀行註冊為根據1956年銀行控股公司法案（Bank Holding Company Act of 1956）及其修正案所設立的財務控股公司。本公司為一間以當地為導向、社區為基礎的金融服務機構，提供包括商業與消費者銀行服務、租賃、信託與投資管理、以及財務規劃與資產管理等完整產品與服務。截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有1間 wholly-owned 銀行子公司，名為Tompkins Community Bank。Tompkins Financial Advisors，為Tompkins Community Bank之一部門，提供完整之投資服務，包括投資管理、信託與遺產規劃、財務與稅務規劃服務。本公司主要辦公室位於紐約伊薩卡市東森納街118號，郵遞區號14850，電話為：(888) 503-5753。本公司普通股於紐約證券交易所美國交易所（NYSE American）交易，代碼為"TMP"。

本年度10-K表報表包含根據1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案（Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995）所定義之「向前看」陳述。本報告中之內容，若非歷史事實陳述，可能包含涉及多種風險與不確定性的向前看陳述。向前看陳述可能以「may」「could」「should」「will」「would」「estimate」「intend」「continue」「believe」「expect」「plan」「commit」或「anticipate」等詞語，以及這些詞語的否定形式或其他類似詞語來識別。向前看陳述的範例可能包括有關本公司貸款組合資產品質的陳述；本公司信用損失準備金的水準；特殊關注與次級貸款相關風險之抵償資產是否充足；流動性來源是否充足；未來期間證券收入的預期；本公司對利率變動及政府/監管預期變更的風險敞口；需在損失回復成本前出售證券的必要性；會計準則變更的影響；趨勢、計畫、前景、成長與策略；未來財務狀況、營運結果、收入、資本支出、成本或其他財務項目之預測；預期的監管與立法變更；以及其它對未來事件或情況的描述，以及其他非歷史事實陳述。向前看陳述是根據管理階層對影響本公司的未來事件的預期與信念所做出，並受到影響本公司營運與總體經濟環境的不確定性與因素影響，這些因素難以預測，且其中許多因素超出本公司的控制範圍，可能導致實際結果與向前看陳述及歷史表現有重大差異。除本報告10-K表報表第1A項所列之風險因素外，以下因素亦可能導致實際結果與向前看陳述及歷史表現有重大差異：總體經濟、市場與監管條件的變動；本公司吸引與留住存款及其他流動性來源的能力；美國國內生產總值（GDP）成長與通貨膨脹趨勢；利率與通貨膨脹環境對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運結果的影響；預期來自本公司業務、投資與貸款活動之其他收入或現金流；影響上市公司、銀行、銀行控股公司與/或財務控股公司的法律與監管變更，包括《多德-弗蘭克法案》（Dodd-Frank Act）及其他聯邦、州與地方政府命令；任何FDIC保險費率變動或與計算FDIC保險費金額相關規則與法規的影響；對金融機構的監督與監管審查變動；科技發展與變更；網路安全事件與威脅；持續以具競爭力的新產品與服務於合時且成本效益的方式推出的能力；政府與公共政策變更，包括環境法規；對大型客戶的依賴；本公司業務的地理集中；以所需金額、時間與條件取得財務資源以支持本公司未來業務的能力；以及國家與全球事件的經濟影響，包括因銀行破產、戰爭與地緣政治問題（包括中東地區持續或升級的衝突與烏克蘭戰爭）、關稅與貿易戰、廣泛抗議、民變、政治不確定性與疫情或其他公共衛生危機所導致的借款人財務壓力、客戶行為變動與信用風險變動。本公司不承擔更新其向前看陳述的義務。
本公司之會計及報導準則，就重大事項而言，符合美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）及財務服務業之一般慣例。在正常營運活動中，管理階層必須選擇並應用許多會計準則與方法，並做出會影響本公司合併財務報表及附註之財務結果之估計與假設。在做出這些估計與假設時，存在固有不確定性，此等不確定性可能對本公司之營運成果與財務狀況造成重大影響。

管理階層認為，若會計估計涉及管理階層需對高度不確定之事項做出假設，則該會計估計對報導之財務結果為關鍵性因素。此外，若管理階層在當期可合理使用不同之會計估計，或在不同期間可能發生合理可能之會計估計變動，而此等變動可能對本公司財務報表產生重大影響，則該會計估計亦被視為關鍵性會計準則。管理階層認為，與信貸減損準備（"準備"，或 "ACL"）相關之會計準則為關鍵性會計準則，因其涉及高度不確定性與主觀性，且與此領域相關之估計對本公司財務狀況與營運成果可能產生重大影響。
本公司用以估計準備之方法，考量與現金流可收回性相關之可用資訊，包括過去事件、當前情況及合理且可支持之預測。請參閱本報告 10-K 表報第 II 項 "項目 8. 財務報表與補充資料" 中 "財務報表附註" 部分之 "準備 for Credit Losses"、"附註 5 - 準備 for Credit Losses" 及 "附註 1 - 重大會計準則摘要"，以取得有關準備之更多討論。
請參閱本報告 10-K 表報第 II 項 "項目 8. 財務報表與補充資料" 中 "財務報表附註" 部分之 "準備 for Credit Losses"、"附註 5 - 準備 for Credit Losses" 及 "附註 1 - 重大會計準則摘要"，以取得有關準備之更多討論。
有關本公司重要會計政策之資訊，以及為更深入瞭解本公司財務表現之報導方式，請參閱本報告表10-K第二部分「第8項 財務報表及補充資料」中「附註1 - 重要會計政策摘要」之內容。

本公司之重要會計政策符合一般會計準則（GAAP），並於本報告表10-K第二部分「第8項 財務報表及補充資料」中「附註1 - 重要會計政策摘要」中說明。在應用這些會計政策時，本公司管理階層需運用判斷以決定許多方法、假設與估計值。某些關鍵會計估計值更依賴此種判斷，且在某些情況下，若因情勢變更而導致假設與估計值改變，可能會導致本公司報導之財務表現出現波動。本公司管理階層應用關鍵假設與估計值最顯著之領域為以下所述：

•信用減損會計處理 - 本公司使用現行預期信用減損模型來處理信用減損準備。根據此模型，信用減損準備代表一個減值帳戶，從某些金融資產（包括貸款與租賃）之攤銷成本中扣除，以反映於資產負債表日預期可收取之淨金額。為調整信用減損準備至管理階層認為必要之水準，會計入信用減損費用。在估計貸款與租賃組合之預期減損時，會使用借款人特定之財務資料與總體經濟假設，以預測合理且可支持之預測期間內之減損。對於某些具有相似風險特徵之貸款組合，本公司會使用統計模型來估計未來現金流、擔保價值及其他用以決定借款人償還義務能力之因素之金額與時間。這些模型考量歷史信用減損與各種總體經濟假設（包括失業率與國內生產總值）之間的相關性。這些預測可能因模型內在限制或偏誤而調整。預測期間之後，本公司會使用較長期歷史減損經驗來估計貸款剩餘合約期間之減損。在決定管理階層之估計值與假設時所考量之情勢變更，可能會導致這些估計值與假設之變更，進而導致未來期間信用減損準備之調整。有關管理階層在決定信用減損準備時所考量之事實與情勢之討論，請參閱本報告表10-K第二部分「第8項 財務報表及補充資料」中「附註5 - 信用減損準備」之內容。

本公司於 2025 年報告的稀釋每股盈餘為 11.24 美元，較 2024 年的稀釋每股盈餘 4.97 美元成長 126.2%。2025 年 12 月 31 日為結算日之年度淨收入為 161.1 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 70.9 百萬美元成長 127.3%。稀釋每股盈餘與淨收入的成長包含將本公司全資子公司 Tompkins Insurance Agencies, Inc. ("TIA") 所發行及流通之資本股票全部出售給 Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC. ("Gallagher")，以約 223.0 百萬美元現金進行交易，扣除慣常之買賣價格調整後，於 2025 年第四季進行。此交易產生稅前獲利 188.2 百萬美元，計入非利息收入。本公司亦因出售 TIA 而產生 4.3 百萬美元之費用，計入非利息費用。部分抵銷 2025 年獲利的是於 2025 年第四季出售 564.2 百萬美元之可供出售債務證券，導致證券出售之稅前虧損為 78.7 百萬美元。管理階層預期此出售將有利於未來期間之證券收入，因所出售證券平均殖利率為 1.56%，而出售所得資金大多數重新投資於殖利率約為 4.52% 之證券。

發行及流通中之本公司全資子公司 Tompkins Insurance Agencies, Inc. ("TIA") 股權，轉讓予 Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC. ("Gallagher")，以約 223.0 百萬美元現金進行交易，並受常見買賣價格調整條款約束，於 2025 年第四季完成。此交易產生預稅獲利 188.2 百萬美元，計入非利息收入。本公司亦因 TIA 股權出售產生 4.3 百萬美元相關費用，計入非利息費用。2025 年部分抵銷此獲利的是，於 2025 年第四季出售 564.2 百萬美元之可供出售債務證券，導致預稅證券出售虧損 78.7 百萬美元。管理階層預期此出售將於未來期間有利於證券收入，因所售證券平均收益率為 1.56%，而出售所得資金大多數重新投資於預估收益率約為 4.52% 之證券。

headings: 本公司可能因擁有之不動產而面臨環境風險及相關成本，這些不動產可能用作本公司貸款之擔保品，或本公司取得其所有權。
過去銀行業之不利發展已對本公司之營運成果及/或股價造成負面影響，未來亦可能造成負面影響。
資產價值下跌可能導致減損費用，並可能對本公司之營運成果、財務狀況及現金流造成不利影響。
本公司業務集中於所經營之總體地理市場，且 largely 依賴這些市場之持續成長與福祉。
本公司之資金來源可能無法足夠取代存款並支撐未來成長。
本公司之流動性可能因其他金融機構之健全性而受到不利影響。
本公司之商譽及其他無形資產減損可能對本公司之財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司依賴其子公司所發放的現金股息以支應其營運，且支付這些股息可能隨時中止。
本公司已遭受到詐欺行為的不利影響，且未來可能持續受到詐欺行為的不利影響。
資訊或其它科技安全的違規，包括因網路攻擊所致，可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
持續且普遍存在的網路安全威脅及事件風險，可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司之業務需要收集及保留大量敏感資料，這些資料受到廣泛的規範與監督，並使本公司業務面臨額外風險。
若本公司之外部供應商未能如預期執行，或本公司無法取得第三方服務，可能對本公司營運造成不利影響。
氣候變遷可能對本公司及其客戶造成重大負面影響。
本公司可能因未能及時偵測並報告洗錢或其他違法活動而面臨法規處罰或責任。
本公司將面臨更高的監管要求及合規成本，隨著本公司總合併資產接近 10 十億美元。
本公司可能涉及訴訟、法律程序、資訊蒐集請求及政府機關或其他當事人之調查，此等情形可能導致不利後果。
本公司面臨收購所帶來的風險，若發生則可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況產生負面影響。
本公司之成功取決於能否為客戶提供持續進化的產品與服務，而本公司可能無法有效管理金融產品與服務開發所內含之風險。
新興與進化的智慧財產權（"AI"）技術之實施與應用，可能帶來不確定性與挑戰。
paragraphs: 本公司之成功取決於管理階層辨識並管理其財務服務業務內在風險之能力。這些風險包括信用風險、市場風險、流動性風險、作業風險、監管、合規及法律風險，以及戰略風險。我們列舉我們所面臨之重大風險。任何這些風險都可能導致對本公司業務、營運結果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流造成重大不利影響，或可能使本公司結果與近期結果，或與本公司所作之任何展望性陳述所暗示之結果有重大差異。
本公司因本公司有相當程度之商業不動產及商業營運貸款集中，而面臨增加之業務風險，這些貸款之償還往往取決於借款人之現金流。

本公司向多種企業提供不同類型之商業貸款，我們認為商業貸款將繼續佔本公司貸款組合之相當大比例，至2026年及以後。不動產貸款一般被視為以擔保為基礎之貸款，貸款金額基於預定之貸款對擔保價值。因此，本公司營運地區之不動產價值下跌將降低這些貸款之擔保價值。此外，本公司已經驗過，並預期將持續經驗商業不動產貸款之競爭增加。此增加之競爭可能抑制本公司產生額外商業不動產貸款或維持現有商業不動產貸款庫存之能力。本公司之商業營運貸款主要基於借款人之現金流及信用worthiness，其次為借款人所提供之擔保財產，而借款人違約時，擔保財產之變現被視為主要之償還來源。借款人之現金流可能難以預測，擔保財產之價值也可能波動。雖然商業營運貸款通常以設備、存貨、應收帳款或其他營運資產為擔保，但在違約時變現擔保財產往往無法提供足夠之償還來源。截至2025年12月31日，商業及商業不動產貸款總計為4.8十億美元，或佔本公司總貸款之73.9%。
本公司之農業貸款往往取決於借款人所在地之農業產業健康狀況，借款人之償還能力可能受許多超出借款人控制之因素影響。

作為本公司商業營運貸款業務之一部分，本公司發放農業貸款，包括農業不動產貸款及農業營運貸款。截至2025年12月31日，本公司總貸款組閤中，農業相關貸款為348.8百萬美元，或佔5.4%，其中包括農業不動產貸款234.3百萬美元及農業營運貸款114.5百萬美元。農業貸款之償還取決於相關農場之成功營運或管理。農場之成功可能受許多超出借款人控制之因素影響，包括不利天氣條件，例如風、冰雹、乾旱及洪水，導致無法種植作物或限制作物收成，牲畜因疾病或其他因素而死亡，農產品市場價格下跌，以及政府規範及補貼（包括價格支持及環境規範之變動）。許多農場依賴有限數量之關鍵個人，若這些個人受傷或死亡，可能對農場之成功營運造成重大影響。若農場營運之現金流減少，借款人償還貸款之能力可能受損。雖然農業營運貸款通常以農場營運資產之廣泛質權為擔保，但任何違約貸款之收回擔保財產可能無法提供足夠之償還來源。

此外，相關農場之營運或管理及價值，受美國政府貿易政策變動之影響。對本公司農業相關貸款所涉及之農場所進口或出口之產品及材料課徵關稅、報復性關稅或其他貿易限制，可能導致相關農場營運及管理成本增加，產品價格上升，需求減少，以及產品邊際利潤下降。此等潛在對農場營運及管理之不利影響，可能降低相關農場之收入、財務結果及償還債務之能力，進而對本公司之財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。此外，若與農業產業相關之政治環境變動對本公司客戶或本公司營運之市場造成負面影響，本公司之業務、營運結果及財務狀況可能於未來受到重大且不利之影響。
